historic/u1e6/anaquito-battle.jpg.description: Labeled sketch 'Batalla del Campo de Anaquito' — the 1546 battle where Gonzalo Pizarro's encomendero rebels defeated Viceroy Blasco Núñez Vela. (554px wide, under the 800px target; the only PD depiction of the battle found.)

historic/u1e6/casta-painting.jpg.description: 18th-century Mexican casta series — 16 labeled panels (e.g. 'Español con India, Mestizo') classifying mixed-race families.

historic/u1e6/debt-peonage.jpg.description: 1910 photograph from John Kenneth Turner's 'Barbarous Mexico' — hundreds of laborers lined up at a Yucatán henequen plantation under a mounted overseer; the classic image of debt peonage.

historic/u1e6/encomienda-workers.jpg.description: 1615 Guamán Poma de Ayala drawing 'Encomendero y familia andina' — a Spanish encomendero with the Andean family under his authority. (Substitution: depicts the encomendero with his charges rather than overseen workers; 651px wide.)

historic/u1e6/hacienda.jpg.description: 19th-century engraving of the hacienda at Uxmal, Yucatán (after Désiré Charnay, 'Ancient Cities of the New World', 1887) — the colonial estate house at the heart of the hacienda system.

historic/u1e6/las-casas.jpg.description: 1886 oil portrait of Bartolomé de Las Casas, Dominican friar and defender of Indigenous rights.

historic/u1e6/middle-passage-ship.jpg.description: The 1789 Brookes slave-ship diagram ('Description of a Slave Ship', British Library) — cross-section and deck plans showing enslaved Africans packed for the Middle Passage.

historic/u1e6/new-laws.jpg.description: Title page of the 1542 Leyes Nuevas ('New Laws') — 'Leyes y ordenanças... para la governacion de las Indias y buen tratamiento y conseruacion de los Indios' — with the imperial arms of Charles V.

historic/u1e6/repartimiento-draft.jpg.description: 1615 Guamán Poma de Ayala drawing (Nueva corónica, p.535) — an Indigenous captain interfacing with a Spanish miner holding ore; the mita/repartimiento draft was organized through Native officials for the mines. (Substitution: no PD Commons image depicts the draft itself; sourced from the Royal Danish Library like E5's Poma drawing; 381px wide.)

historic/u1e6/sao-tome-sugar.jpg.description: Frans Post, 'Engenho de açúcar' (c. 1664) — a Brazilian sugar mill (engenho) with workers. (Substitution: no PD São Tomé-specific image found; the Brazilian engenho is the same plantation-mill complex pioneered on São Tomé.)

historic/u1e6/silver-mine-workers.jpg.description: Theodor de Bry engraving (c. 1590, after José de Acosta) — Indigenous workers climbing ladders and laboring in the Potosí silver mines. Distinct from E5's four Potosí images; intended as the E5 callback.

historic/u1e6/sugar-cane-cutting.jpg.description: William Clark, 'Slaves cutting the sugar cane' (1823), plate IV of 'Ten Views in the Island of Antigua' (British Library) — enslaved workers harvesting cane under an overseer on horseback.

historic/u1e6/las-casas-engraving.jpg.description: 1665 German edition illustration of Las Casas: the Dominican who gave back his encomienda in 1514

historic/u1e6/hacienda-mexico.jpg.description: Ex-hacienda San Antonio, Acolman: the great estate where debt, not chains, bound the peons

historic/u1e6/mexican-peon.jpg.description: Barbarous Mexico (1911): peon laborers — technically free, bound by unpayable debt

historic/u1e6/casta-panel.jpg.description: 'De mestindio y castiza produce coyote': casta panel naming and ranking the mixtures

historic/u1e6/guaman-poma-page.jpg.description: Guamán Poma's chasqui (1616): an Indigenous nobleman's drawn testimony of colonial rule

historic/u1e6/gonzalo-pizarro.jpg.description: 1851 illustration of the severed heads of Gonzalo Pizarro and Carbajal: the encomendero rebellion that killed the king's viceroy at Añaquito in 1546

historic/u1e6/hacienda-workers.jpg.description: Grinding cacao at La Chonita Hacienda, Tabasco: the hacienda economy that replaced the encomienda

historic/u1e6/mexico-city.jpg.description: Colonial building in Mexico City's historic center: the viceregal capital that ran the repartimiento
